---
id: SA-0413
title: "The unreviewed witness watches only result.verdicts, so a guard built from a trimmed numbering never shows"
type: bug
priority: 2
risk: standard
estimated_lines: 19
estimate_measured: true
touches:
  - tests/test_rebut.py
forbidden:
  - DESIGN.md
  - CONTEXT.md
  - CLAUDE.md
  - README.md
  - pyproject.toml
  - uv.lock
  - .saffron/**
  - .claude/**
  - ontology/**
  - tests/ontology/**
  - docs/**
  - images/**
  - harness/**
  - records/**
  - hooks/**
  - saffron/**
  - tests/test_review.py
  - tests/test_session.py
budget_usd: 10
max_attempts: 2
max_turns: 60
acceptance:
  - claim: >-
      `run_rebut` builds `numbered = list(enumerate(blockers, 1))` once
      (saffron/phases/rebut.py:919) and, after the verdict loop, calls
      `guarded = _guarded_blockers(numbered, acceptance)` unconditionally
      over that same full `numbered` (saffron/phases/rebut.py:1046), never
      over `mine`, the per-lens subset the loop narrows to
      (saffron/phases/rebut.py:1021). `_guarded_blockers` builds its
      returned dict one entry per pair in its first argument, each decided
      from that pair alone (saffron/phases/rebut.py:602-607), so trimming
      that argument changes the dict's size but never a surviving entry's
      own value. `_check_withdrawal_refusals` reads `guarded.get(verdict.finding)`
      only for a finding that produced a `Verdict`
      (saffron/phases/rebut.py:628-629), one whose lens is not in
      `unreviewed`. So `result.verdicts` cannot tell the real build apart
      from one that drops a named lens's own pairs from `numbered` before
      that call. A spy that replaces `rebut._guarded_blockers` and records
      `len(numbered)` on every call
      `test_a_lens_named_unreviewed_gets_no_verdict_session_and_keeps_its_numbers`
      makes must record `len(blockers)`, 2, on each of its six calls,
      whatever `unreviewed` names and whichever blocker it names.
    witness: tests/test_rebut.py::test_a_lens_named_unreviewed_gets_no_verdict_session_and_keeps_its_numbers
    preserves: true
    wrong_versions:
      - "The guard is read over the numbering with the named lenses' blockers dropped."
      - "The guard is read over the numbering accumulated from `mine` as the verdict loop builds it, so a lens left out of the loop leaves its own blockers out of the guard too."
---

## Context

Backlog-tracked finding on `SA-0406`'s own rebuttal record, read at the
origin head `403d8a40`. `SA-0406`'s criterion 3 claims a witness. That
witness,
`test_a_lens_named_unreviewed_gets_no_verdict_session_and_keeps_its_numbers`
(tests/test_rebut.py:2423), guards the wrong version "The guard is read
over the numbering with the named lenses' blockers dropped." It does
not. `_guarded_blockers` computes its dict entry by entry. Each entry is
independent of which other entries are present
(saffron/phases/rebut.py:584-608). `_check_withdrawal_refusals` only ever
consults the entry for a blocker that produced a `Verdict`. That is a
blocker whose lens the verdict loop did not skip
(saffron/phases/rebut.py:611-628, 1016-1019). Across every case the test
builds, dropping some other blocker's pair from the list passed to
`_guarded_blockers` changes nothing. No assertion on `result.verdicts`
the test makes can see it. The in-cell rebuttal record for that wrong
version argued this exact point. It claimed a fix: "a spy on
`rebut._guarded_blockers` that records the length of its first
argument." No such spy, or any other internal-contract check, exists in
`tests/test_rebut.py`. None exists at either the origin head or the
current head `6a8cc298`. CLAUDE.md's own convention says a witness is
not trusted until it fails against the unfixed build it is meant to
catch. This one does not.

The guard's own behavior reads over the full `numbered`, never a
trimmed form of it. That already holds at both the origin head and the
current head. The gap is only that no witness checks it as an internal
contract. This criterion is declared `preserves: true`: the witness
already exists under this name, and it already passes. The change only
strengthens its body, so it stays green before and after.

## Problem

Add the spy the rebuttal record promised and never landed, so criterion
3's own wrong version is caught.

1. Give the existing test a `monkeypatch` parameter.
2. Before the `cases` loop, keep the real `rebut._guarded_blockers` and
   build a list `guard_calls`. Install a replacement on `rebut` that
   appends `len(numbered)` then delegates to the real function.
3. After the test's last assertion, assert `guard_calls` holds
   `len(blockers)` once per call the test makes: once per case in the
   loop, once for `result_default`, once for `reordered`.

No other assertion in the test changes. No production file changes: the
behavior the claim describes is already correct at the current head, and
stays that way.

## Out of scope

- **A fix to `saffron/phases/rebut.py`.** It already reads the guard over
  the full `numbered`, line 1046. Nothing here edits it.
- **A new predicate or keyword.** `run_rebut`'s own signature,
  `_guarded_blockers`'s own signature, and every other test in
  `tests/test_rebut.py` stay as they are.
- **The other allowed test files.** Neither `tests/test_review.py` nor
  `tests/test_session.py` holds any part of this gap.
- **A rename.** The test keeps its name. The `census` gate reads a
  renamed test as a removed one.

## Notes for the agent

**The spy.** `monkeypatch` is pytest's own fixture, already used across
the suite, for example `tests/test_cli.py:592`. No import beyond it is
needed. Keep the spy's own function short. It takes `numbered` and
`acceptance`, appends `len(numbered)` to the outer list, and returns the
real function's own result. Every existing assertion on the result stays
valid.

**Where the six calls come from.** Four inside the `cases` loop
(tests/test_rebut.py:2447-2460 at the head cited above), one more for
`result_default`, one more for `reordered`. `blockers` holds two findings
throughout, so `len(blockers)` is 2 at every call, including the
`reordered` case, which passes `[healthy, guarded]`, still length 2.

**Why `preserves: true`.** The witness name already exists at the
commit this spec is written at, since `SA-0406` added it. The criteria
gate's own direction rule treats a witness green at base as proof of
nothing, unless the criterion says the opposite on purpose. This one
does: the guard's own behavior already holds, and the strengthened test
is expected to stay green on both sides of this diff. `SA-0280`'s
`test_the_policy_template_names_every_policy_field` criterion is the
same shape, a `preserves: true` criterion carrying its own
`wrong_versions`.

**Measured.** A prototype on the current head added 18 lines and removed
1 in `tests/test_rebut.py`, 127 changed tokens, against the `bug` ceiling
of 1300. `ruff format` and `ruff check` passed on it. The full
`tests/test_rebut.py` suite, 68 tests, passed on it.
`saffron/phases/rebut.py`'s guard call was changed to read over
`numbered` filtered to drop any lens named in `unreviewed`. On that
change, the witness failed with `guard_calls == [1, 1, 1, 0, 2, 1]`
against the expected `[2, 2, 2, 2, 2, 2]`. With it changed instead to
accumulate the guard's argument from `mine` as the verdict loop builds
it, the witness failed the same way. Reverted to the current head, the
witness passed again.

**Prose.** The two new comments read 23 and 17 words, each one sentence,
no em dash, no semicolon, no contraction.
